title: Fundamental groups commute with algebraic constant-field limits
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $L/K$ a separable algebraic extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $K$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For each intermediate field $K\subseteq E\subseteq L$ with $[E:K]<\infty$, put $X_E=X_0\times_K E$, and put $X_L=X_0\times_K L$ [def-pc-base-change]. Assume that $X_L$ and every $X_E$ are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and choose a geometric point $\bar x\to X_L$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Give each $X_E$ the composite point $\bar x_E$. Use the profinite fundamental groups of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. The homomorphisms induced by the projections [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] give an isomorphism of topological groups
$$\pi_1(X_L,\bar x)\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{[E:K]<\infty}\pi_1(X_E,\bar x_E).$$
The transition homomorphism for $E\subseteq E'$ is induced by $X_{E'}\to X_E$. The inverse limit means the subgroup of compatible families in the product, with its subspace topology, and the displayed map has components induced by $X_L\to X_E$.

proof.text: Use the recorded finite-etale fibre functors directly. IsFundamentalGroup identifies each group model with its natural automorphisms via toAut_bijective and with its topological automorphism group via toAutHomeo. Finite intermediate fields have common finite upper bounds by the finite-dimensional compositum instance. No passage to finite locally constant sheaves is required.

proof.text: Construct transition fibre isomorphisms from pullbackFiberIso and the composition equation for fieldExtensionBaseMap. Their pointwise first-projection equation is immediate. Pullback pasting and naturality of the G_L action imply compatibility of the coordinate fundamentalGroupMaps. Thus the product-coordinate homomorphism R takes values in the stated infimum of equalizer subgroups and is continuous coordinatewise.

proof.text: If R(g)=1, descend each cover P to a finite intermediate field using object descent. fundamentalGroupMap_smul shows g acts trivially on that pullback. Naturality along the model isomorphism gives trivial action on P. The non_trivial axiom of IsFundamentalGroup gives g=1.

proof.text: For a compatible family a, conjugate the natural automorphism given by its E-coordinate along pullbackFiberIso, giving an automorphism A_E of the pulled-back fibre functor. The projection identity for a pullback-pasting comparison e and fundamentalGroupMap_smul imply e intertwines A_E and A_Eprime. This applies also to the comparison isomorphisms furnished by morphism descent, whose projection equations are part of its statement.

proof.text: A morphism between models over one field descends after enlargement. Its descended naturality equation transports along the comparison isomorphisms, so A_E commutes with every morphism between its limit models. Models over distinct fields are compared at their finite compositum using canonical pullback-pasting isomorphisms. Hence every morphism between any two limit models intertwines their component automorphisms.

proof.text: Choose a descended model for each cover P. Conjugate A_E by the fibre of the model isomorphism to get an automorphism of F(P). The previous all-models naturality equation, applied to the comparison morphism between any chosen pair, proves naturality. Applied to a comparison with an already descended object it proves the expected component formula. toAut_bijective supplies the corresponding g in G_L; fundamentalGroupMap_smul and that component formula give R(g)=a. Together with injectivity this makes R a group isomorphism.

proof.text: Each G_E is Hausdorff because toAutHomeo identifies it with the Hausdorff automorphism group of its finite-etale fibre functor. The product and its compatible-family subgroup are Hausdorff. A continuous bijection from compact G_L to that subgroup is a homeomorphism. Its forward map is definitionally R, so the required coordinate equation holds by reflexivity.

lean.note: The limit is the infimum of equalizer subgroups of the product, with inherited subtype topology. The existential transition fibre isomorphisms are uniquely specified on every point by their projection equation, so their fundamentalGroupMaps are the canonical transition maps. The last equation specifies the canonical limit map on every coordinate. Small fundamental-group models use the established IsFundamentalGroup interface.
